overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance over the past 30 days reveals that space exploration, extreme planetary conditions, and high-stakes 'What If' scenarios dominate engagement velocity. Specifically, recent 7-day content featuring bizarre planetary traits (e.g., Venus's day/year ratio, liquid diamond planets, and extreme precipitation types) achieves significantly higher views-per-day and like-to-view ratios compared to general animal facts or psychological tricks. The audience heavily favors visually striking, counter-intuitive cosmic concepts with rapid-fire pacing under 21 seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (970 views in <2 days) and 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1024 views) show massive breakout velocity and strong like-to-view conversion.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space scenarios and weird physics of celestial bodies, focusing on impossible-sounding planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles challenging conventional timelines or physical perceptions (e.g., TrES-2b dark planet with 1026 views) outperform standard informational summaries.
winning_patterns.action: Use high-contrast conceptual hooks that pit familiar objects against cosmic extremes.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal human psychology or memory tricks (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', songs stuck in head) consistently flatline below 60 views over extended periods.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological hacks and brain teasers unless they tie directly into high-concept neuroscience or mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic biological facts without a narrative or existential threat (e.g., standard octopus or jellyfish facts) yield low engagement velocity compared to dynamic space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content entirely toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary adaptations rather than simple trivia.

next_video.concept: What happens if Earth passes through a rogue magnetic filament?
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-sentence with an immediate visual of auroras completely engulfing the night sky in broad daylight.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that every compass on Earth would instantly spin backward and fry every electrical grid within minutes before humanity even realized why.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' space format while introducing a fresh, urgent Earth-bound physics threat that drives high retention and comment speculation.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not use diamonds, rain, sharks, or time dilation
Must focus on a completely unmentioned celestial/geophysical phenomenon

experiment: A/B test a pure cosmic physics mystery ('What If') against a cinematic animal survival scenario using identical thumbnail framing and rapid-fire audio pacing to determine secondary niche viability.
